pr_title: fix(core): Access injected parent values using SkipSelf
pr_body:
In ViewEngine, SelfSkip would navigate up the tree to get tokens from
the parent node, skipping the child. This restores that functionality in
Ivy. In ViewEngine, if a special token (e.g. ElementRef) was not found
in the NodeInjector tree, the ModuleInjector was also used to lookup
that token. While special tokens like ElementRef make sense only in a
context of a NodeInjector, we preserved ViewEngine logic for now to
avoid breaking changes.

We identified 4 scenarios related to @SkipSelf and special tokens where
ViewEngine behavior was incorrect and is likely due to bugs. In Ivy this is
implemented to provide a more intuitive API. The list of scenarios can be
found below.

1. When `Injector` is used in combination with `@Host` and `@SkipSelf`
on the first Component within a module and the injector is defined in the
module, ViewEngine will get the injector from the module. In Ivy, it does
not do this and throws instead. [Test](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/39464/files#diff-ece22a8d8ae1405b0b70f8824055ccc962cd82206fcdc9932dfd754885e31be3R798)

2. When retrieving a `@ViewContainerRef` while `@SkipSelf` and `@Host`
are present, in ViewEngine, it throws an exception. In Ivy it returns the host
`ViewContainerRef`. [Test](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/39464/files#diff-ece22a8d8ae1405b0b70f8824055ccc962cd82206fcdc9932dfd754885e31be3R1378)

3. When retrieving a `@ViewContainerRef` on an embedded view and 
`@SkipSelf` is present, in ViewEngine, the ref is null. In Ivy it returns the
parent `ViewContainerRef`. [Test](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/39464/files#diff-ece22a8d8ae1405b0b70f8824055ccc962cd82206fcdc9932dfd754885e31be3R1083)

4. When utilizing `viewProviders` and `provider`s, a child component that is
nested within a parent component that has `@SkipSelf` on a `viewProvider`
value, if that provider is provided by the parent component's `viewProviders`
and `providers`, ViewEngine will return that parent's `viewProviders` value,
which violates how viewProviders' visibility should work. In Ivy, it retrieves
the value from `providers`, as it should. [Test](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/39464/files#diff-ece22a8d8ae1405b0b70f8824055ccc962cd82206fcdc9932dfd754885e31be3R1574)

These discrepancies all behave as they should in Ivy and are likely bugs in
ViewEngine.

## PR Type
What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.io application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:


## What is the current behavior?
Currently Ivy ignores @SkipSelf entirely, which deviates from ViewEngine and expectations of behavior.

Issue Number: [34066](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/34066), [34819](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/34819)

## What is the new behavior?
@SkipSelf now properly navigates up the view tree to find the correct injected resource in the parents.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Closes #34066, #34819.

issue_context.title: In Ivy, SkipSelf() is not accessing the parent's ViewContainerRef, ElementRef, etc
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by Angular Ivy ### Description Before Ivy, I was able to access the `ViewContainerRef`, `ElementRef`, etc of the parent directive using the `@SkipSelf` decorator in the child directive. With Ivy integrated in my project, it's no longer skipping its own injections and accessing the ones in its parent. For example, I have the following code: In app.component.ts ```ts @Directive({ selector: '[parentDirective]' }) export class ParentDirective { constructor(private vc: ViewContainerRef){ console.log(vc.element); } } @Directive({ selector: '[childDirective]' }) export class ChildDirective { constructor(@SkipSelf() private vc: ViewContainerRef){ console.log(vc.element); } } ``` in app.component.html ```html
parent child
``` These two directive classes should log the same ViewContainerRef element. However, with Ivy, you can see that's no longer the case. Here is the [reproduction](https://ivy.ng-run.com/edit/xMfu7xoF1t4b8hFvoU9N?open=app%2Fapp.component.html). This reproduction is made in Angular Ivy 8.1.0-next.3. But I also see this behavior in my project that's on "@angular/core": "9.0.0-rc.3", ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction [Minimal Reproduction](https://ivy.ng-run.com/edit/xMfu7xoF1t4b8hFvoU9N?open=app%2Fapp.component.html) ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 


"@angular/core": "9.0.0-rc.3",
comments: Note: When trying to fix this, we realized that it's non-trivial because of the way Ivy is architected. We should consider whether this is actually a feature we want long-term due to the design / performance cost.

@kara - RE "whether this is actually a feature we want long-term due to the design / performance cost" - Please see my comments on #39475

In short, [HostBindings not updated by detectChanges() in OnPush component](22560) (or detached components) is a real problem, and the workaround for that requires accessing the parent view's ChangeDetector. 

Personally I think the HostBindings update design is a root problem (it should be possible to update classes tied to property values without jumping through hoops or understanding things like "hostbindings aren't updated by a view's detectChanges()") - I don't know how many other common use-cases there are requiring core parameter types from the node's parent, but my guess is that if that design were fixed, the need for this would be dramatically reduced.

Also, if injectflags are not supported, there should be a compiler or runtime error.
FYI, this issue is resolved by #39464 and the fix will be available in v11.0.0. Thank you.
